title: The Agentic Loops Every Developer Should Know
abstract: Loops are a key primitive for autonomous AI agents, and the now widely used "Agent Mode".
This session dives into the journey from the core Reason + Act loop to loop engineering — the shift from prompting agents to designing the systems that prompt them.
And while the loops run — and the lights go out on fully automated Dark Software Factories — what should we focus on?

resources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models (Yao et al.)
resources.note: The paper behind the Reason + Act loop.
resources.note_pt: O artigo por trás do loop Reason + Act.

resources.title: Behavior, Purpose and Teleology (Rosenblueth, Wiener & Bigelow, Philosophy of Science, 1943)
resources.note: The 1943 paper that explained purposeful behavior as negative feedback, the root of cybernetics.
resources.note_pt: O artigo de 1943 que explicou o comportamento com propósito como feedback negativo, a raiz da cibernética.

resources.title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models (Huang et al.)
resources.note: How the model gets feedback from its environment on every step.
resources.note_pt: Como o modelo recebe feedback do ambiente a cada passo.

resources.title: The Law of Leaky Abstractions (Joel Spolsky)
resources.note: Why every abstraction, agents included, eventually leaks.
resources.note_pt: Porque é que todas as abstrações, incluindo os agentes, acabam por deixar escapar o que escondem.

resources.title: The Five Levels: from Spicy Autocomplete to the Dark Factory (Dan Shapiro)
resources.note: A ladder of AI coding autonomy, up to the lights-out software factory.
resources.note_pt: Uma escada de autonomia na programação com IA, até à dark software factory.

resources.title: Loop Engineering (Addy Osmani)
resources.note: Designing the loops that prompt coding agents.
resources.note_pt: Desenhar os loops que dão prompts aos coding agents.

resources.title: What is loop engineering? (The Pragmatic Engineer)
The Factory Model: How Coding Agents Changed Software Engineering (Addy Osmani)
resources.note: Building the factory that builds your software.
resources.note_pt: Construir a fábrica que constrói o teu software.

pt.title: Os loops agênticos que todos os programadores devem conhecer
abstract: Os loops são uma primitiva fundamental dos agentes de IA autónomos e do agora amplamente usado "Agent Mode".
Esta sessão percorre o caminho desde o loop base Reason + Act até ao loop engineering — deixar de escrever prompts para os agentes e passar a desenhar os sistemas que os escrevem.
E enquanto os loops correm — e as luzes se apagam em Dark Software Factories totalmente automatizadas — em que nos devemos focar?

title: From Copilot to Autopilot: The Two AI Loops Every Developer Should Know
summary: Most AI coding is still single-turn autocomplete. Agents work in loops. The session covers two of them, ReAct (the agent loop) and RALPH (plan, execute, verify, reset, repeat), with live demos, how agents fail, where humans approve, and a developer playbook built on context and spec-driven engineering.

pt.title: Do Copilot ao Autopilot: os dois loops de IA que todos os programadores devem conhecer
pt.summary: A maior parte da programação com IA ainda é autocomplete de um só passo. Os agentes trabalham em loops. A sessão mostra dois deles, o ReAct (o loop do agente) e o RALPH (planear, executar, verificar, recomeçar, repetir), com demos ao vivo, as formas como os agentes falham, onde entra a aprovação humana e um guia prático assente em context engineering e spec-driven development.
